entries.name: Filesystem
entries.blurb: Read and write files under directories you name, with the paths checked against that list.

inputs.label: Directory it may reach
inputs.help: An absolute path. The server refuses anything outside it, so this is the whole of what it can see. Add more by hand in the command line below.

entries.name: Git
entries.blurb: Read history, diffs and blame in a repository, and stage and commit in it.

entries.name: Fetch
entries.blurb: Fetch a web page and convert it to markdown for the model to read.

entries.name: Memory
entries.blurb: A knowledge graph the model can write to and read back across conversations.

entries.name: Sequential thinking
entries.blurb: A scratchpad for working a problem in steps, revising earlier ones as it goes.

entries.name: Time
entries.blurb: The current time, and conversion between timezones.

inputs.label: Local timezone
inputs.help: An IANA name such as Europe/London. Leave the argument off entirely — delete it below — to let the server read the system clock's.

entries.name: GitHub
entries.blurb: Issues, pull requests, code search and Actions, against GitHub's own hosted server.

inputs.label: Personal access token
inputs.help: A fine-grained token, scoped to the repositories you want reachable. GitHub's server also speaks OAuth, which Taurus cannot do yet — a token is the way in.

entries.name: Brave Search
entries.blurb: Web, news and image search through Brave's own index.

inputs.label: API key
inputs.help: From the Brave Search API dashboard. The free tier is enough to try it.

entries.name: PostgreSQL
entries.blocked: There is no first-party Postgres server to recommend. The reference one was archived in May 2025 and deprecated on npm in July 2025 over a SQL-injection vulnerability, and nothing official replaced it. The maintained alternatives are all third-party, which is exactly the package-name-nobody-reviewed problem this catalogue exists to avoid — so pick one yourself, read it, and add it by hand.

entries.name: Google Drive
entries.blurb: Search and read files in Drive.
entries.blocked: Google runs a hosted server at https://drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1, and it authenticates with OAuth against credentials you create in your own Google Cloud project. Taurus speaks HTTP to a server with fixed headers and has no OAuth flow, so there is nowhere to put the consent step. The reference Drive server that predated Google's is archived and should not be used.

entries.name: Linear, Sentry, Stripe, Notion, Cloudflare
entries.blurb: Vendor-hosted servers for issue trackers, payments and docs.
entries.blocked: All of these are hosted by the vendor and secured with OAuth rather than a token you can paste. Taurus sends fixed headers and has no consent flow, so none of them can be reached yet. Where a vendor also issues a plain API token, the HTTP form below will take it.

entries.name: Slack
entries.blocked: The reference Slack server is archived and is now maintained outside the project. Slack's own replacement is hosted and OAuth-secured, which Taurus cannot do yet. Add a third-party one by hand if you have read it.
